title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: -364 poultry, fruit and vegetable Small and Micro Enterprises (SMEs) were established, and jobs created for 1555 (975F) unemployed youth in Amhara and Sidama Regions. -ILO entrepreneurship and business skills development training tools such as GET Ahead, and SIYB methodologies development tools adapted and rolled out by the Bureau of job creation, the Bureau of livestock and pastoralist resources, and the Bureau of cooperatives in the refugee and host communities of the Somali Regional State of Ethiopia. -571 refugees in Addis Abeba, as well as in the Somali region were supported in accessing financial services to start and run small businesses. -The Ethiopian Kaizen Excellence Centre provided SCORE training and advisory services to 40 SME S collectively employed more than 3,000 workers. LLPI-RDC and TGI-RDC, supported 20 enterprises using the ILO SCORE approach. Through this partnership the technical capacity of 15 staff members from both partners developed to continue providing the service continuously. -The ILO SCORE productivity endeavour also extended its reach to universities, including HU, BDU, and ASTU. These institutions were equipped with SCORE Training of Trainers (TOT), empowering 25 professionals to subsequently guide 40 enterprises in boosting their productivity and competitiveness. -EHPEA, HCCSA, ACSA and BCCSA received ILO support to implement SCORE productivity intervention. 23 dedicated professionals have been deployed by these partners who are now providing training and advisory services to 40 enterprises. -3,000 potential and returned migrants trained using the SIYB and financial education tools. -2,000 potential and returned migrants established enterprises or accessed wage employment in Ethiopia. The ILO supported 24 experts (21 F) cooperative authorities' provision of training on ILO cooperatives training material; Ethiopian Kaizen Excellence Center provided Productivity and OSH for 20 medium and large Agri business enterprises employees in Amhara and Sidama regions; the establishment of a National Business Development Services Provider Association in forcibly displaced communities, including the development of bylaws and access to registration license, contributing to operationalizing the Ethiopia's Comprehensive Refugee Response Framework; TOT to 150 (30% female) SCORE trainers that cascaded to 151 enterprises, which employed over 30,000 workers, with 87% of the workers being female; capacity building interventions to engage dairy processors and build milk cooling facilities; 500 refugees and HC; financial education to 500 beneficiaries; design and facilitate business plan competition; the development of cooperative societies in the dairy value chain in Jigjiga and Kebribeyah; adaption of SIYB tool to the features of potential and returned migrants and additonal modules and sections with food processing industry, which was further translated into Amharic and rolled out in Addis Ababa, Amhara, and Oromia regions, and certified 16 national trainers and trained 284 (231 F) potential and returned migrants; 29 (8 F) experts from Amhara and Sidama regions received training on SIYB and 234 entrepreneurs (78 MSMEs) were trained on fruits, vegetables, and poultry sector; adaption of translated financial inclusion booklet; 628 (565 F) potential and returned migrants benefitted and 8 trainers certified as national ILO financial education trainers; provision of a comprehensive economic assistance to 1,152 (926 F) potential and returned migrants; their sustainable integration into the labour market; 632 (329 F) benefited from the ILO revolving loan (800,000USD) in Addis Ababa, Amhara and Oromia regions.
